chunks: Ibn Qulawayh from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari from his father from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab said: Yuzayd ibn Ishaq narrated to us from Harun ibn Hamzah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him: Two people from the People of the Book, either two Christians or two Jews, had a dispute between them, and a judge from among their judges ruled between them with injustice. The one against whom the ruling was made refused to accept it and asked to be referred to the judge of the Muslims. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is referred to the judge of the Muslims.'

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ: People of the Book (Christians and Jews)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when a non-Muslim disputes a judgment from their own judge in Islamic law?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the mechanism of *taqlid* in judicial matters, affirming that non-Muslims may voluntarily submit to Islamic courts (*hukm al-Muslimin*) for a binding decision, particularly when seeking relief from their own judges' injustice. This principle underscores the comprehensive authority of Islamic law (*Sharia*) and the validity of cross-community legal recourse in classical Shia jurisprudence.
